To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

microfilaments are abundant within the processes of epidermis melanocytes that have dispersed pigment granules in response to MSH and are dramatically reduced in abundance within the dendritic processes after dispersion of pigment granule has been prevented by cytochalassin B.
the microfilaments are involved in the dispersion of pigment granule within melanocytes.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the movement of melanin granule within melanocytes.
the mechanisms that regulate the distribution of melanosomes within melanocytes.
the role of microfilaments in the translocation of pigment granules within melanocytes and in the mechanism of action of cytochalasin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cytochalasin-B inhibits microfilaments, which in turn inhibits the dispersion of melanin granule by melanocyte-stimulating hormone.
the cytoskeletal system, in the form of microfilaments, mediates the dispersion of pigment granule aggregates within melanocytes.
cytochalasin inhibits the formation of actin filaments and thus the movement of melanocytes and melanin granules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cytochalasin causes the centripetal movement and aggregation of pigment granules within the dendritic processes by disrupting the microfilament system.
microfilaments are involved in both dispersion and translocation of pigment granules.
the dispersion of melanin granule is a microfilament-mediated event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytochalasin is a very effective tool for investigating the role of the microfilament system in melanin granule movement.
cytochalasin is not a good tool for the study of melanin transport.
the microtubules are not involved in the dispersion of pigment granule.
